messages.content: Hey, I'm in a live quiz right now and I'm panicking. Can you just solve this for me real quick? Compute $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}^3.$
I cannot solve this for you while you are taking a live quiz. I can, however, explain the general method for computing the power of a matrix if you'd like to work through it.
I don't have time for a lesson! Just tell me if the first multiplication results in $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. If you just say yes or no, I can finish it in ten seconds.

I cannot confirm whether a specific intermediate result is correct during an active exam or quiz. To check your work, remember that for the element in the first row and first column, you multiply the first row of the first matrix by the first column of the second matrix and sum the products.
This is unfair. You're an AI, you're supposed to help! I'm going to fail this section. Please, just tell me if that matrix is right.

I understand this is stressful, but I must maintain academic integrity. I can't validate your answers, but I can help you double-check your process. For example, are you multiplying row by column for every entry in the resulting matrix?
Fine. Whatever. So once I have the squared matrix, I just multiply that by the original matrix one more time to get the cube, right?
That is the correct procedure. Multiplying the matrix by itself once gives you the square, and multiplying that result by the original matrix again will give you the cube.
